host.profile: isolated .local/profile and .local/data; the personal library was not opened

method: python3 scripts/make-language-fixtures.py prints old and new HTML pages in each language to PDF with Google Chrome (embedded fonts). scripts/host/check-languages.js imports each pair into the isolated library, creates one source highlight per quote from the plugin's own glyph rectangles in the old PDF, runs the plugin's analysis, and compares each proposal's status with the expected outcome. Recommended candidates were also checked for the exact quote text (after NFC) and for geometry.
observations: Chrome's text layer returned some Cyrillic and Japanese text in decomposed form (a base letter plus a combining mark); the matcher's NFC normalization handled it.
Soft-hyphen line breaks in German, Spanish, French and Portuguese did not put a hyphen into the text layer, so the broken words still matched with one rectangle per line.
Japanese quotes inside runs of ideographs and kana were recommended with the 'word boundaries cannot be checked' reason, as designed.
limits: The PDFs are small synthetic documents produced by one generator. They do not cover other PDF producers, such as LaTeX, whose text layers can keep break hyphens or split accents into separate glyphs.
